Thus far Beza. In vvhich vvordes he vnvvittingly, but mo{{ls}}t truely, iu{{ls}}tifieth and defendeth the old vulgar Tran{{ls}}lation again{{ls}}t him {{ls}}elf and al other cauillers, that accu{{ls}}e the {{ls}}ame, becau{{ls}}e it is not al waies agreable to the Greeke text: Vvhereas it vvas tran{{ls}}lated out of other Greeke copies (partly extant, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Vvhen the Fathers {{ls}}ay, that the Latin text mu{{ls}}t yeld to the Greeke, & be corrected by it, they meane the true and vncorrupted Greeke text.}}partly not extant at this day) either as good and as auncient, or better and more auncient, {{ls}}uch as S. Li. 2. de doct. Chri{{ls}}t. c. 15.''

And if it were not to long to exemplifie and proue this, which would require a treati{{ls}}e by it {{ls}}elf, we could {{ls}}hew by many and mo{{ls}}t cleere examples through out the new Te{{ls}}tament, the{{ls}}e {{ls}}undrie meanes of iu{{ls}}tifying the old tran{{ls}}lation.

Fir{{ls}}t, if it agree with the Greeke text (as commonly it doth, and in the greate{{ls}}t places cōcerning the controuer{{ls}}ies of our time, it doth mo{{ls}}t certainely) {{ls}}o far the Aduer{{ls}}aries haue not to complaine: vnles they wil complaine of {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The vulgar Latin Tran{{ls}}lation, is many Waies iu{{ls}}tified by mo{{ls}}t auncient Greeke copies, & the Fathers.}}the Greeke al{{ls}}o, as they doe Ia. 4. v 2. and 1 Pet. 3. v. 21. where the vulgar Latin foloweth exactly the Greeke text, {{ls}}aying, ''Occiditis:'' and, ''Quod vos {{ls}}imilis formæ,'' &c. But Beza in both places correcteth the Greeke text al{{ls}}o as fal{{ls}}e.

If the{{ls}}e marginal Greeke copies be thought le{{ls}}{{ls}}e authentical then the Greeke text, the Aduer{{ls}}aries them {{ls}}elues tel vs the cōtrarie, vvho in their tran{{ls}}lations often folow the marginal copies, and for{{ls}}ake the Greeke text. as in the examples aboue mentioned Ro. 11. 4. If al Era{{ls}}mus Greeke copies haue not that which is in the vulgar Latin, Beza had copies which haue it, and tho{{ls}}e mo{{ls}}t auncient (as he {{ls}}aith) & better. And if al Bezas copies faile in this point and wil not helpe vs, Gagneie the Frenche kings preacher, and he that might commaund in al the kings libraries, he found Greeke copies that haue iu{{ls}}t according to the vulgar Latin: & that in {{ls}}uch place as would {{ls}}eeme otherwi{{ls}}e le{{ls}}{{ls}}e probable. as Iac. 3. ver{{ls}} 5.
